records.authority_name: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)
records.licensing_notes: Confirmed directly: 'worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use the Information, including for commercial purposes'. Requires source attribution; excludes third-party IP, official symbols/marks. Clean and strong — comparable to UK OGL.
records.notes: No REST API — official annual downloadable Excel/PDF release from cbsa-asfc.gc.ca (structured, not scraped: a first-party file, same authoritative-manual/file-ingest pattern as TARIC, not the interactive-HTML-scraping this project refuses to do). Every record reportedly carries MFN, General Tariff rate, unit of measure and multiple FTA preferential-rate columns per line, suggesting good preference/RoO-adjacent representation once parsed.

records.authority_name: Japan Customs — Customs and Tariff Bureau, Ministry of Finance
records.update_cadence: twice yearly (Jan 1 / Apr 1), archived by date
records.licensing_notes: No licence text located in this pass. Japan Customs publishes distinct dated schedule pages (each release keeps its own URL, e.g. /2026_04_01/), which is unusually good for effective-date/history modelling even without a formal API — but redistribution terms need direct confirmation before building anything.
records.notes: e-Stat (e-stat.go.jp) has a real API but for TRADE STATISTICS, not the tariff schedule itself — do not conflate the two. The tariff schedule is structured HTML/PDF per dated release.

records.authority_name: Australian Border Force (ABF) — Department of Home Affairs
records.licensing_notes: Not located this pass.
records.notes: ABF's Trade Data API Services are for cargo/logistics status (ICS), NOT tariff lookup — do not conflate. The 'Working Tariff' is PDF-delivered, chapter by chapter. tradeapi@abf.gov.au was surfaced as a contact point for scoping what's actually available; not pursued further this pass.

records.authority_name: New Zealand Customs Service
records.licence_name: Listed on data.govt.nz as 'Other (check with source agency)'
records.licensing_notes: The DATASET listing on data.govt.nz explicitly does not carry a standard open licence — it defers to the New Zealand Customs Service. This must be confirmed directly with Customs before building anything; do not assume data.govt.nz's general open-data reputation extends to this specific dataset.
records.notes: Best-documented small-market candidate technically (real API access via data.govt.nz's registry, 24-hour refresh) — gated entirely on a licence confirmation email/call, not on engineering.

records.authority_name: Korea Customs Service (KCS)
records.update_cadence: unknown for HSK classification data; monthly for a separate trade-statistics API found in the same portal
records.licensing_notes: IMPORTANT: KOGL has MULTIPLE TYPES. The confirmed general rule is 'works shall be used only for nonprofit purposes... it is possible to use for commercial purpose with special permissions' — commercial use is NOT the default; it requires per-dataset special permission from the issuing institution. Do not assume the HSK classification dataset carries the permissive KOGL type without checking its specific type tag on data.go.kr.
records.notes: Real open-API infrastructure exists (data.go.kr, RestAPI JSON/XML, registration required). The blocker is entirely the KOGL-type-per-dataset licensing question, not technical access.

records.authority_name: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) — Tares
records.licensing_notes: CONFIRMED, not inferred: opendata.swiss states attribution is required AND 'commercial use requires permission from the data owner'. This is the same shape of blocker that disqualified WTO — a real API exists, but written permission is a precondition, not a formality. Classified D_blocked pending that permission, exactly as WTO is in unconfigured-sources.ts.
records.notes: Technically the best-documented candidate researched (JSON/XML API, opendata.swiss metadata). Blocked purely on licence, the same category as WTO — should follow the identical pattern in unconfigured-sources.ts rather than being silently skipped.

records.authority_name: Israel Tax Authority — Customs
records.update_cadence: 'several times a day' per the query portal
records.licensing_notes: Not located this pass.
records.notes: Downloadable rate files (PDF, by appendix) plus an interactive query portal (shaarolami-query.customs.mof.gov.il) updated intraday. No public API found; the query portal is exactly the kind of interactive interface this project treats as out of scope unless it is documented as an API.

records.authority_name: Dubai Customs (federal Integrated Customs Tariff shared across GCC states)
records.licence_name: UAE Federal Open Data License (Dubai Pulse)
records.licensing_notes: CONFIRMED: 'free to exploit the information for both commercial and non-commercial purposes' with attribution to the Dubai Government, no misleading/deceptive use, no implication of official endorsement, and images/trademarks excluded. This is one of the strongest licensing findings in this pass — genuinely comparable to UK OGL. NOT YET CONFIRMED: whether the specific customs-tariff dataset on Dubai Pulse (linked above) actually carries this exact license versus a narrower one — the general Dubai Pulse platform terms were confirmed, the dataset-specific page was not individually re-checked.
records.notes: Also relevant: an AI-powered HS classification tool ('Al Munasiq') exists but is a web tool, not evidenced as an API for bulk/programmatic tariff retrieval. The GCC 12-digit harmonisation (rolled out UAE-wide from Aug 2025) means a UAE parser's SHAPE would likely transfer to Saudi/Kuwait/Qatar/Bahrain/Oman with national override work — but each state still publishes and administers its own schedule; see source-families.md, GCC.

records.customs_union_or_regional_family: MERCOSUR (shared nomenclature and base tariff, national administration and exceptions)
records.authority_name: Receita Federal / Portal Único de Comércio Exterior (Siscomex)
records.licensing_notes: Not located this pass. Brazilian federal public-sector data is often released under generically-open terms in principle, but this was not confirmed for Portal Único specifically.
records.notes: The Portal Único de Comércio Exterior exposes an API used by at least one third-party classification vendor (SAP) for its product-attribute catalogue — evidence an API surface exists, though its scope, auth model and licence were not directly confirmed. TEC/LETEC: Brazil (and other MERCOSUR members) can carry national exceptions to the shared TEC via LETEC, so a Brazil parser is NOT automatically an Argentina/Paraguay/Uruguay parser — see source-families.md, MERCOSUR.

records.authority_name: Secretaría de Economía — SIAVI / SAT (TIGIE)
records.licensing_notes: Not located this pass.
records.notes: SIAVI (Sistema de Información Arancelaria Vía Internet) is a Spanish-language web platform, no API found. USMCA relevance is high for a fuller North American picture alongside Canada/US, but current evidence supports web-interface acquisition only.

records.customs_union_or_regional_family: Türkiye–EU Customs Union (goods scope, not TARIC access)
records.authority_name: Ministry of Trade — General Directorate of Customs (Türkiye)
records.licensing_notes: Not located this pass.
records.notes: Tariff Nomenclature is downloadable position-by-position from the General Directorate's Data Bank; also a Binding Tariff Information (BTI) online service. No API found. Türkiye is in a goods customs union with the EU, but this does NOT mean TARIC access covers Turkish national administration — Türkiye maintains its own tariff and non-EU-origin duties separately.

records.authority_name: General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China (GACC)
records.licensing_notes: No licence text found. PRC government data licensing is not presumed open by default the way UK/Canada/US government data is; do not infer permission from the mere existence of a public lookup tool.
records.notes: China Customs Tariff Lookup System is a web search tool. No API found. Politically and commercially significant for Indian trade context but rated lower automation feasibility than most peers and carries the highest unverified-licensing risk of the large economies researched.

records.authority_name: South African Revenue Service (SARS)
records.licensing_notes: Not located this pass.
records.notes: Schedule 1 Part 1 (the tariff book) is a 700+ page PDF, ~11,876 active codes — this is the authoritative-manual-release pattern (like TARIC/CBSA), not scraping, but a much larger manual-parse effort. Schedule also carries anti-dumping/countervailing duties (Schedule 2) — genuine trade-remedy coverage if parsed. SACU leverage: see source-families.md.

records.destination_country: GCC family (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman)
records.authority_name: No single GCC-level authority publishes tariff data; each member administers nationally
records.licensing_notes: See per-country entries. UAE is the licensing bright spot of the group; Saudi is confirmed blocked; Kuwait/Qatar/Bahrain/Oman unresolved.
records.notes: FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (Part 3): the 12-digit code STRUCTURE is genuinely harmonised across the six states since the 2025 rollout, so a parser built for one member's schedule shape is materially reusable for another's — but there is no single machine source. Each state remains its own acquisition target, its own licensing question, and its own national-override layer (excise, VAT, national prohibitions all differ). Do NOT count this as 'one adapter unlocks 6' — count it as 'one shared parser design, six separate acquisitions.'

records.authority_name: No single MERCOSUR-level machine source; TEC/NCM shared, national administration and LETEC exceptions
records.licensing_notes: Not located at family level; Brazil's own portal not yet confirmed either.
records.notes: FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (Part 3): TEC exists and the NCM 8-digit nomenclature is genuinely shared, so classification-refinement concordance work transfers across members. But LETEC lets any member run national exceptions to the TEC, so a tariff RATE from Brazil's schedule cannot be assumed to apply in Argentina/Paraguay/Uruguay without checking that country's own exception list. Preferences and quotas: not confirmed centralized or national this pass. Treat as nomenclature-level leverage only, not a single acquisition target.

records.destination_country: ASEAN AHTN family (Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Brunei, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar)
records.customs_union_or_regional_family: ASEAN (not a customs union — a shared nomenclature only)
records.authority_name: No shared tariff authority; each member administers nationally under the common AHTN nomenclature
records.licensing_notes: Not located at family level.
records.notes: DISCOVERED IN RESEARCH, not in the task's explicit family list, but structurally identical in kind to MERCOSUR: ASEAN is not a customs union (no common external tariff and no centralized preferences/quotas), only a shared 8-digit nomenclature base (AHTN) that each of 10 members extends and administers independently, with independently negotiated FTA schedules. Genuine leverage is at the classification-concordance layer only. Do not treat as a customs-union-style single source.

records.destination_country: EAEU family (Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan)
records.authority_name: No single public EAEU-level tariff database confirmed
records.licensing_notes: Not located.
records.notes: FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (Part 3): CONFIRMED — 'there is no single official public database at the EAEU level' for export duties, and none for preferential rates either. Common Customs Tariff exists as approved Commission decisions, not as a queryable database. Fully fragmented to national administrations. Russia carries independent, severe sanctions/geopolitical risk that makes this family a non-priority regardless of data availability — recorded for completeness, not recommended for any near-term wave.

records.destination_country: ECOWAS family (Nigeria, Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal + 11 others)
records.customs_union_or_regional_family: Economic Community of West African States
records.authority_name: ECOTIS (ECOWAS Trade Information System); national administration
records.licensing_notes: Not located.
records.notes: FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (Part 3): a real 5-band CET structure (0/5/10/20/35%) exists and Nigeria/Ghana both confirmed implementing it, but the ECOTIS portal shows policy documentation rather than a confirmed machine interface, and national tariff-line extensions/exceptions were not confirmed to be shared. Treat as nomenclature/band-structure leverage only, with high per-country acquisition effort.

records.destination_country: EAC family (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, DR Congo)
records.authority_name: eac.int (policy publication); national administration
records.update_cadence: unknown, gazetted revisions (e.g. annual Finance-Act-style CET amendments)
records.licensing_notes: Not located.
records.notes: FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (Part 3): a genuine 4-band CET (0/10/25/35%, expanded from the original 3 bands in 2022) with gazetted council decisions, but no confirmed database or API — gazette-notice-based. National tariff-line extensions and duty remissions vary by member. Low near-term priority given acquisition tier.

records.authority_name: SARS (South Africa) administers the shared external tariff other members apply
records.licensing_notes: See South Africa entry; not independently confirmed for the other four members.
records.notes: FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (Part 3): SACU is the ONE African-bloc case researched where a single member's schedule (South Africa's) is genuinely applied by the others as their external tariff by design — this is real leverage, unlike ECOWAS/EAC/MERCOSUR/GCC/ASEAN. What still needs a national-override layer, per the task's own question: each of Botswana/Eswatini/Lesotho/Namibia can levy its own VAT/excise and maintains its own import-control/licensing regime, and BLNS-specific rebate provisions exist — so 'apply South Africa's rate' is a strong default, not an unconditional one. This is the single best candidate for 'one adapter, several destinations, with a defined override layer' found in this pass.
